topic: Analyzing device session data and traffic discrepancies
summary_markdown:
The conversation focused on advanced SQL queries for analyzing device session data across multiple facilities and sensors. Initial discussion involved selecting sessions and devices starting at similar times across different sensors, leading to the development of optimized SQL queries using `device_id`, `vendor_id`, and time grouping (`toStartOfFiveMinute`).

Later, a major task was completing the migration/recalculation of 'Mall' data for Lithuania (Литва). The initial date used (June 7th) was determined to be incorrect, requiring recalculation.

A separate technical discussion addressed discrepancies in total traffic when comparing aggregated 'Mall Master Facility' data versus summing individual screen facility data. It was explained that selecting the master facility causes sessions to merge (cluster), while selecting screens individually results in simple summation, leading to expected differences.
decisions: The 'Mall' data for Lithuania must be recalculated using correct dates/methods.
A query structure grouping by `device_id`, `vendor_id`, and time bucket was finalized for efficient session analysis.
action_items: Investigate the source of traffic discrepancies between master facility aggregation and individual screen summation.
Follow up on fixing data inconsistencies, noting potential impact on existing data.
